name: PieChart
intent: How a whole splits into a few parts, as a donut or a solid pie, like payments by method.
usage: Use PieChart for the share of a total across a handful of parts. It is one component: pass data, one entry per slice. Slices go largest first from the top, clockwise; past maxSlices the rest merge into one grey Other slice. donut (the default) leaves a hole with the total in it; turn it off for a solid pie. The legend lists each part with its percent, beside the chart or under it. Hover or use the arrow keys for a tooltip with the value. animate sweeps the slices in. ChartTone: green | olive | cyan | orange | pink | gray | purple | yellow | red | mint (the kit category colors). title and subtitle write a heading over the chart; showTitle turns it off when the Card around it already says the same. See contracts/piechart.json for the full contract.

label.note: Names the chart for screen readers and captions its data table.

title.note: Visible title over the chart, like Revenue by period. The screen-reader name still comes from label.

subtitle.note: A quieter line under the title, like Last 12 months, all accounts.

showTitle.note: Shows the title and subtitle. Off draws the chart alone, when the Card or Section around it already carries the title.

data.itemShape: { label: string; value: number; tone?: ChartTone }
data.note: One entry per slice. Zero and negative values are left out.

donut.note: A ring with the total in the middle. Off draws a solid pie.

showTotal.note: The total and totalLabel in the donut's hole.

showLegend.note: Each part with its color and percent.

legend.note: Legend beside the chart or under it.

maxSlices.note: The most slices; past it the smallest merge into Other.

otherLabel.note: The name of the merged slice.

animate.note: The slices sweep in. Always off when the person prefers reduced motion.

useWhen: The share of a total across 2 to 6 parts: payments by method, revenue by region.
doNot: Do not use it for many parts or values over time. Use BarChart or LineChart.
Do not use it to compare parts that don't add up to a whole.
Do not draw charts with loose SVG or a chart library. Use the kit charts.
Do not use raw hex; pick a tone.
a11y: A figure named by label. The drawing is hidden from screen readers; a visually hidden table lists each part with its value and share.
The chart takes focus: the arrow keys move from slice to slice and show the tooltip. Escape hides it.
The legend names every color with its percent, so color is not the only way to tell slices apart.
The sweep is subtle and optional (animate), and never plays when the person prefers reduced motion.
snippet:
<PieChart
  label="Payments by method"
  data={[
    { label: "Card", value: 182400 },
    { label: "ACH", value: 96300 },
    { label: "Wire", value: 41800 },
  ]}
  format="currency"
/>

examples.title: Donut
examples.usage: The total in the middle, the legend with percents beside it.

examples.title: Pie with the legend below
examples.usage: donut off draws a solid pie; legend bottom puts the parts under it.
